Abstract 
Artificial intelligence can produce polished se-
mantic artefacts before their sources, transfor-
mations, limits, and authorized uses are 
reconstructable. This monograph treats that prob-
lem as a sequence rather than a pile of theories. 
Reticular Local Abstraction (RLA) is used as a 
general grammar for a scientific commonplace: 
the same domain is represented at multiple levels, 
and every transmission preserves some distinctions 
while collapsing others relative to declared ques-
tions. Compact Reticular Computabil ity (CRC) 
then asks when such a multi -level description has 
actually been compiled into an effective, bounded 
computational object. A literature -compiled bry-
ophyte model supplies the stress case: when equa-
tions, parameters, taxonomic scope, or calibration 
are incomplete, the act of compilation exposes 
approximations and transfers that must either re-
main declared or become hidden epistemic liabili-
ties. From that hinge, epistemic convolution is 
defined as a CNN -inspired movement over se-
mantic fields - local operators, aggregation, col-

lapse, candidate stabilization, and typed non -
answer - without claiming a new neural primitive. 
Reticular Observer Architectures (ROA) formal-
ize the resulting bounded observer: horizon, retic-
ulum, local transducers, memory, monitoring, 
receipts, validation, and human authority. Epis-
temic Debt is the accounting consequence: un-
paid warrant attached to semantic objects before 
use, while a separate named -use gate decides 
whether residual debt is tolerable, review -
requiring, waived, or blocking. An optional 
bounded-simulation bridge to cellular automata 
remains outside the causal spine. The formal core 
mixes credited standard results, local derivations, 
non-entailments, and conditional conformance 
invariants; the debt vector remains a candidate in-
strument; empirical superiority, independent peer 
review, proof -assistant verification, calibration, 
dependency completeness, and institutional legit-
imacy remain open. The programme should be 
simplified or rejected if matched, simpler baselines 
deliver equal reconstruction and protection 
against unsupported authoritative use at lower 
burden.

Significance and Scientific Contri-
bution 
The core problem is not merely that AI can emit 
false sentences. It is that any representation can 
become actionable before the warrant for its use is 
reconstructable. The proposed architecture joins 
abstraction, computability, typed refusal, prove-
nance, assurance, and use -sensitive governance 
without collapsing them into one score. Its 
strongest claim is conditional and testable: making 
horizon, lineage, debt, and gate outcomes first -
class should reduce unsupported authoritative use 
and reconstruction cost relative to simpler base-
lines, while preserving human accountability. The 
maturity ledger above is binding: candidate com-
positional contribution, constructibility, and in-
ternal consistency are not substitutes for 
instrument reliability, empirical validation, or in-
dependent authority.

The Wager in One Page 
A machine can now produce a polished answer 
before an institution can reconstruct how that an-
swer was made. The old problem of knowledge is 
that every map leaves something out; the new op-
erational problem is that machines can draw and 
circulate maps faster than people can recover what 
was omitted, borrowed, approximated, collapsed, 
or never checked. The failure is therefore larger 
than false sentences. It is semantic work becoming 
actionable before its warrant is reconstructable. 
This book names the unpaid remainder Epis-
temic Debt. A claim, label, summary, model, 
equation, or risk object carries debt when some 
warrant required to understand or rely on it re-
mains unresolved: source, trace, transformation, 
collapse, label, reification, validation, authority, or 
transfer. Debt is not a synonym for falsehood. A 
statement may be true and still carry debt because 
its path cannot be reconstructed; an approxima-
tion may be useful and honest when declared, yet 
hazardous when promoted as established fact 
without provenance or validation.

## Page 20

The Accounting Laye r of Computationa l Semantics  
20 
The companion operation is a bounded seman-
tics of claim admissibility. Under a declared hori-
zon of sources, scope, transformations, receipts, 
support rules, validations, and resource limits, a 
system can compute what status a claim has 
earned and can return answer, unknown, contra-
diction, review, timeout, failure, or out-of-horizon 
rather than manufacturing completion. That 
computation does not decide truth. It makes the 
observer and its limits explicit. 
The wager is therefore modest and testable: if 
representations carry their own horizon, lineage, 
unresolved debt, and use boundary, machine -
assisted work should become easier to reconstruct 
and harder to launder into unsupported authori-
ty. If simpler provenance, assurance, selective -
prediction, or workflow systems achieve the same 
protection with less burden, this architecture 
should contract to those simpler forms.

A Scene Before the Theory 
A compliance team asks an AI system to summa-
rize supplier-payment controls. The output states 
that payments above a threshold require approval 
by the chief financial officer. The sentence is plau-
sible and immediately reusable, but an auditor 
asks: which interview or policy supports it, what 
population it covers, whether exceptions were 
tested, what transformation produced the word-
ing, and who reviewed the conclusion. If those 
questions cannot be answered, the defect is not 
merely possible hallucination; it is unreconstruc-
table semantic work. The surface is ready before 
the warrant is. 
Now move the same problem into science. A 
literature compiler needs a physiological relation 
for a bryophyte model. The relevant literature 
may supply a species -specific equation, a range, a 
qualitative dependency, a relation measured in a 
nearby taxon, or no directly usable function at all. 
The honest description is not one exclusive label 
but a small profile: source_basis records whether 
support is DIRECT, TRANSFERRED,

## Page 24

The Accounting Laye r of Computationa l Semantics  
24 
 SYNTHESIZED, or UNRESOLVED; com-
piler_ops records every declared operation applied 
by the compiler, including approximation when 
one is introduced; calibration_state records what 
has actually been calibrated or tested. A trans-
ferred relation can therefore also be approximated, 
and a direct relation can still be unvalidated for 
the intended conditions. Failure begins when one 
of those dimensions is silently omitted or promot-
ed into a stronger evidential state. 
This is the bridge from CRC to Epistemic 
Debt. Compiling a scientific domain does not 
manufacture missing science; it reveals where a 
computable reticulum needs more warrant than 
the literature presently supplies. An AI system can 
make that gap more dangerous because it can gen-
erate a plausible bridge. The architecture does not 
claim to eliminate such bridges. It requires them 
to carry their papers.

The Seven Questions 
1. What does a representation preserve, and for 
which questions? RLA supplies a common 
grammar for stating the answer. 
2. When does a collection of models become an 
executable object? CRC requires effective opera-
tors, scheduling, resource bounds, terminals, and 
explicit failure. 
3. What happens when the science does not sup-
ply every required equation or parameter? The 
bryophyte case separates source basis, compiler 
transformations, calibration, and unresolved re-
lations so approximation and transfer can re-
main inspectable obligations rather than 
mutually exclusive labels. 
4. How can AI assemble and navigate semantic 
structure without pretending to be a new neural 
theory? Epistemic convolution reuses the local -
operator / aggregation / collapse gesture while 
keeping candidate and certified objects distinct.

## Page 26

The Accounting Laye r of Computationa l Semantics  
26 
5. What is the observer? ROA is the bounded 
contract that joins horizon, reticulum, local op-
erators, receipts, memory, monitoring, valida-
tion, and human authority. 
6. What remains unpaid after a semantic 
transformation? Epistemic Debt records the un-
resolved warrant component by component; it 
does not estimate truth. 
7. Who finally decides whether the object may be 
used? A named -use gate evaluates debt and evi-
dence under a governance context; waiver per-
mits without paying, while discharge changes the 
evidence state.

How to Read This Book 
The book can be read linearly without prior 
knowledge of the ROA corpus. The main thread 
is a genealogy of different object types, not six 
theories competing at the same level: a scientific 
grammar, an executability criterion, a stress case, a 
semantic compilation method, an observer archi-
tecture, and an accounting discipline. Formal 
readers can descend into the local theorem chap-
ters; other occasional readers can follow the chap-
ter questions, running examples, and boundary 
boxes. Every load -bearing claim is tagged by what 
it is: definition, credited standard result, local der-
ivation, conditional conformance invariant, em-
pirical target, implementation witness, or open 
problem. 
Two sentences to carry. A representation is useful 
because it leaves something out; it becomes dan-
gerous when its omissions are spent as warrant. 
ROA constructs the bounded observer, and Epis-
temic Debt records what its semantic artefacts 
still owe before use.

CHAPTER 1  
Every Representation Pre-
serves Some Distinctions 
and Loses Others 
What is lost whenever anything is represent-
ed? 
On the wall of almost every classroom hangs a lie. 
The world map we grew up with shows Green-
land roughly the size of Africa. In truth Africa is 
about fourteen times larger. The map is not mis-
taken — it is a Mercator projection, built in 1569 
to do one thing supremely well: let a sailor draw a 
straight line and hold a true compass bearing 
along it. To buy that gift, the map gives some-
thing up. It stretches the far north and south, 
swelling Greenland and shrinking the tropics. The 
distortion is not an error. It is a choice — a partic-
ular human point of view, made for a particular 
purpose. 
A representation is useful because it leaves 
something out. A map cannot keep every property 
of the territory. A scientific model cannot keep

## Page 38

The Accounting Laye r of Computationa l Semantics  
38 
every feature of the system. A legal memo cannot 
keep every possible reading. A dashboard cannot 
keep all the evidence behind a score. The loss is 
not the failure; the failure begins when the loss is 
forgotten. 
So the correct question about a representation 
is not whether it is false, but what it was made for 
and what it cannot support. A navigation projec-
tion may be excellent for bearings and poor for 
comparing the area of continents. Used for the 
second purpose, it is being pushed beyond the 
warrant it earned. Epistemic Debt names exactly 
that excess of use over warrant. 
The debt is not always a lie. It may be a missing 
caveat, a lost scale, a summary without source 
density, a label that grew too broad, or a model 
rule whose empirical status is unclear. Error sug-
gests a binary defect; debt names a use -
independent obligation attached to an object un-
der a horizon. The same debt vector can be tolera-
ble for orientation and blocking for authoritative 
use because the gate, not the vector, is use -

CHAPTER 2  
Why Artificial Intelli-
gence Makes an Old Epis-
temic Problem 
Operationally Urgent 
Why does a very old epistemic problem be-
come urgent now? 
Humans have always summarized, classified and 
inferred. What changed is speed, volume and in-
stitutional dependence. An AI system now pro-
duces policies, risk objects, scientific syntheses, 
legal issue lists, code reviews and board memos 
faster than review structures can reconstruct their 
evidence paths. The most visible failure is halluci-
nation, but it is not the deepest one. The deeper 
failure is unreconstructable semantic work: a pol-
ished artefact exists, but the organization cannot 
say which source suppor ts each claim, what was 
inferred, which caveats were lost, who reviewed 
the conclusion, or what residual risk was accepted. 
The output survives; the warrant trail evaporates.

## Page 43

The Accounting Laye r of Computationa l Semantics  
43 
This moves the problem from private virtue to 
public infrastructure. It is no longer enough for a 
careful person to know a claim is uncertain. The 
uncertainty must travel with the artefact. A sys-
tem must be able to represent not only an answer 
but also unknown, contradiction, review -
required, out -of-scope and debt -bearing states — 
so that machine-assisted work accumulates instead 
of evaporating. 
The central acceleration is not only that AI 
writes faster. It is that AI can produce socially us-
able surfaces - summaries, labels, tables, decisions, 
risk categories - before anyone has reconstructed 
their source chain. That inversion changes the 
governance problem: review arrives after use un-
less the proof object travels with the claim — 
sources, receipts, transformations, debt vector, 
and the identifier of the horizon they were com-
puted under, so status can be recomputed rather 
than assumed. 
Reader payoff: this chapter is not only about 
hallucination. It reframes hallucination as one case 
of a larger institutional problem: semantic surfac-
es become actionable before their warrant be-

## Page 44

The Accounting Laye r of Computationa l Semantics  
44 
comes reconstructable. Once that is clear, the rest 
of the monograph can stop chasing every possible 
model failure and focus on the status layer that 
should travel with every output. 
A particularly revealing special case appears 
when AI is used to compile science. If a required 
relation is unavailable in usable form, a model may 
offer a plausible proxy, transfer a relation from a 
nearby organism or scale, or synthesize a func-
tional form from several sources. None of those 
moves is automatically a hallucination. The epis-
temic failure is the undeclared promotion: an ap-
proximation, transfer, or synthesis presented 
downstream as if it were a directly sourced, locally 
validated relation. The bryophyte case later makes 
this distinction concrete.

CHAPTER 3  
Epistemic Status Without 
Ontological Overreach 
Does the system decide what exists, or only 
what may be used? 
This monograph lives on the epistemological side. 
It is about the status of claims and artefacts — 
what is supported, unsupported, contradiction, or 
out-of-scope, and what it still owes — not a theo-
ry of what ultimately exists. When a system de-
fines an object called invoice, species, risk, control, 
hormone or legal issue, it has not discovered the 
furniture of reality; it has declared a working vo-
cabulary for a horizon. 
The computational semantics of claim admissi-
bility therefore computes admissibility. It answers 
a restricted question: given these sources, this 
scope, these transformations, these receipts, this 
support matrix and these validation predicates, 
what state may this claim carry now? The disci-
pline protects both sides. It guards against naive 
automation, where a computed answer is treated

## Page 47

The Accounting Laye r of Computationa l Semantics  
47 
as true, and against sterile scepticism, where every 
imperfect representation is dismissed as useless. 
The Unintegrated Problem Across 
Adjacent Research Fields 
The programme stands downstream of mature 
traditions. Information theory explains limits on 
transmission and compression; sufficient statistics 
and Blackwell comparison formalize task -relative 
informativeness; abstract interpretation provides 
sound abstraction of program semantics; comput-
ability theory bounds effective procedures; simu-
lation and bisimulation specify cross -system 
correspondence; selective prediction and confor-
mal methods formalize abstention and risk con-
trol; paraconsistent logic and argumentation treat 
contradiction; provenance standards record deri-
vation; assurance cases organize claims, argu-
ments, and evidence; proof -carrying code attaches 
certificates to artefacts; model cards, datasheets, 
FactSheets, and algorithmic audits document in-
tended use and risk; philosophy of science sup-
plies model -relative representation, severe testing, 
and social criticism.

No novelty is claimed for those components. 
The differential claim is architectural. Existing 
disciplines usually answer different questions: 
what information was lost?; what program property 
is soundly approximated? ; which conclusion sur-
vives attack?; where did the data come from? ; may 
the classifier abstain? ; does the safety argument 
support the claim?  ROA/ED attempts to keep 
these questions typed but connected across one 
lifecycle: a representation is constructed under a 
horizon, transmitted across levels, executed by lo-
cal units, challenged by terminal states, persisted 
with provenance, assigned unpaid warrant, and 
finally compared with a named use at a gate. 
The selected neighbours constrain the contri-
bution claim. RLA must not be presented as re-
placing abstract interpretation, information 
bottleneck, sufficient statistics, causal abstraction, 
or coarse-graining. CRC must not be presented as 
a new computability thesis. ECNN must not be 
reduced to neural uncertainty or allowed to bor-
row the maturity of selective prediction. The op-
tional bounded -simulation bridge must use 
ordinary simulation obligations when invoked.

reconstruction quality while weakening refusal 
behaviour, so semantic recoverability cannot be 
treated as behavioural or governance preservation 
(Nguyen and Lin, 2026). Local diagnostic regions 
can reveal where a causal abstraction succeeds ra-

with abstentions exposes a formal trade -off be-

validate the architecture. 
New work is not promoted into a new ROA 
layer merely because it is newer, more capable, or 
more mathematically expressive. It is first typed by 
the interface it changes: abstraction and fidelity 
belong at RLA; executability, tools, memory, 
scheduling, and resource control at CRC/ECU; 
model-side uncertainty at the epistemic head; as-
surance, monitoring, provenance, and threat ar-
guments at ROA; residual warrant at Epistemic 
Debt; permission at the named-use gate. A com-
parator changes the mandatory spine only when it 
reconstructs one of those interfaces with equal or 
greater diagnostic power at lower burden; other-
wise it is a stronger local formalism, an input sig-
nal, an implementation pattern, or an empirical 
baseline. This rolling rule lets the literature grow 
without turning literature growth into ontology 
growth.

What is inherited, what is relabeled, and 
what is actually claimed as new? 
The framework is strongest when it refuses novel-
ty by vocabulary. Levels, abstractions, partitions, 
sufficient statistics, coarse -graining, simulation 
relations, partial functions, provenance graphs, 
abstention, assurance cases, technical debt, and 
human authorization all have mature scientific 
homes. The contribution claimed here is therefore 
neither a new law of nature nor the discovery of 
these ingredients. It is a typed composition that 
makes their interfaces explicit and attaches use -
sensitive unpaid warrant to the semantic objects 
that cross them. The layer notes below state se-
lected neighbours, the relabeling risk, the claimed 
delta, and the condition under which the delta 
should be rejected.

CHAPTER 5  
From Generated Answers 
to Explicit Bounded Ob-
servers 
What is missing when an answer arrives 
without its observer? 
The bottleneck in AI -assisted work is no longer 
fluent generation; it is reconstruction, prove-
nance, proof and governance. A prompt -first 
workflow generates a convincing report, analysis 
or compliance artefact, but afterwards an organi-
sation often cannot say which evidence supported 
each claim, what was inferred rather than sup-
ported, what was missing, or whether the result 
was approved, merely reviewed, or only drafted. 
The dominant pattern prompt → answer hides 
the observer behind the answer. The observer -
compiler picture is different. Many of the most 
useful outputs of AI work are not final answers 
but intermediate, typed artefacts — definitions, 
taxonomies, blueprints, issue chains, graph frag-
ments, challenge suites, review checklists — which

## Page 66

The Accounting Laye r of Computationa l Semantics  
66 
a human curator corrects, compresses, validates 
and reuses as input for later steps. Cumulative in-
telligence is not located inside a single model call; 
it is distributed across calls, human decisions, files, 
versions, traces and reviews. A prompt, on this 
reading, is the design of a natural -language opera-
tor over a field, not a request for a sentence. This 
monograph proposes a shape that makes that 
structure explicit: bounded domain material → 
explicit observer structure → typed epistemic ar-
tefacts → validation state → proof / witness / re-
view / governance. A reticular observer 
architecture is a finite, horizon -relative structure 
specifying what can be represented, how distinc-
tions are transmitted or collapsed, which artefacts 
can be produced, and under which validation and 
governance conditions they may be used.

CHAPTER 6  
Computational Semantics 
of Claim Admissibility 
Within a Declared Epis-
temic Horizon 
What, exactly, is claimed to be computable? 
The framework uses “computational semantics” 
in a deliberately restricted sense. Classical opera-
tional semantics maps programs to transition be-
haviour; denotational semantics maps expressions 
to mathematical objects; axiomatic semantics re-
lates programs to assertions (Scott and Strachey, 
1971; Plotkin, 1981/2004; Hoare, 1969; Winskel, 
1993). Here the object is different: a versioned 
claim or semantic artefact under a declared hori-
zon. The local computation maps that object to 
an evidence status, debt vector , typed terminal, 
and receipt. Formally, for a horizon H and claim 
c, CS_H(c) = ⟨status_H(c), debt_H(c), termi-
nal_H(c), receipt_H(c) ⟩ when the admitted

## Page 70

The Accounting Laye r of Computationa l Semantics  
70 
source enumeration, transformations, support 
rules, validation predicates, scheduler, and 
timeout policy are effective. This is a semantics of 
admissibility and use -readiness, not a universal 
semantics of truth. Answer, unknown, contradic-
tion, out -of-horizon, review -required, timeout, 
and failure are all successful typed outputs when 
produced by the declared rules.  The claim is con-
ditional. A semantic operation is computational 
only after the state representation, admitted oper-
ators, stopping conditions, failure constructors, 
and resource envelope are declared. The architec-
ture therefore rejects a common equivocation: a 
finite vocabulary does not make an evaluation 
computable, and a computed status does not 
make the represented claim true. Computability 
belongs to the evaluator; warrant belongs to evi-
dence and use; truth remains external to the 
framework. 
What must be declared before a system is al-
lowed to answer? 
A horizon is not a poetic boundary. It is an op-
erational contract. It declares which sources are 
admitted, which scope is in force, which trans-

## Page 71

The Accounting Laye r of Computationa l Semantics  
71 
formations are allowed, which receipts count, 
which support -and-contradiction matrix is used, 
and which validation predicate must hold before a 
claim can move to a stronger status. 
Without a horizon, semantic computation in-
flates: the system answers as if every possible 
source, law, theory and reviewer were available. 
With a horizon, it knows what it is allowed to 
know and what it must mark out -of-scope. The 
horizon also makes disagreement intelligible: two 
reviewers may assign different statuses to the same 
claim because they work under different admitted 
sources or scope. That is not a bug when the hori-
zon difference is declared; it is the condition that 
makes status computable. 
The horizon is deliberately contractual because 
a system cannot compute the status of a claim un-
til it knows which sources count, which transfor-
mations are allowed, which receipts are required, 
which standards apply and which uses are exclud-
ed. “Answer the question” is not yet a computable 
instruction; “answer under this horizon and re-
turn a status” is.

Gödel boundary. Let F be a consistent, effectively 
axiomatized formal theory capable of representing 
elementary arithmetic. Gödel’s first incomplete-
ness theorem implies that F is incomplete: some 
arithmetical sentence is not decided by F. Under 
the usual derivability conditions, the second theo-
rem prevents F from proving its own consistency 
if it is consistent (Gödel, 1931). These results con-
cern sufficiently expressive formal theories; they 
do not show that every practical model is incom-
plete, that empirical evidence is futile, or that a 
machine can never prove useful theorems. Their 
architectural consequence is narrower: internal 
derivability cannot be promoted into a complete 
certificate of truth.

## Page 78

The Accounting Laye r of Computationa l Semantics  
78 
Church–Turing boundary. Church and Turing 
established equivalent formal accounts of effective 
calculability and undecidable decision problems 
(Church, 1936; Turing, 1936/1937). In modern 
terms, no total computable procedure decides the 
halting behaviour of every program -input pair. A 
bounded observer therefore needs resource budg-
ets, timeout,  and non -answer terminals. Hiding 
nontermination behind a spinner or a guessed an-
swer is not semantic completion. 
Rice boundary. Rice’s theorem states that every 
non-trivial extensional property of the partial 
function computed by an arbitrary program is 
undecidable (Rice, 1953). The qualifier exten-
sional matters: syntactic properties and many 
properties over restricted finite domains remain 
decidable. ROA therefore does not claim a univer-
sal checker of “meaning.” It checks declared pred-
icates over typed, bounded objects; when a 
requested property escapes that contract, the cor-
rect result is out -of-horizon, timeout, review, or 
an explicit open proof obligation. 
Shannon boundary. Shannon entropy quanti-
fies uncertainty in a distribution and supports rig-

## Page 79

The Accounting Laye r of Computationa l Semantics  
79 
orous accounts of coding, channel capacity, and 
information loss (Shannon, 1948). It does not by 
itself encode reference, truth, justification, author-
ity, or intended use. RLA can use entropy and 
mutual information to measure preservation un-
der a distribution, but Epistemic Debt is not en-
tropy: it records unpaid warrant, including 
source, validation, authority, and transfer obliga-
tions that may remain high even when a represen-
tation is information-rich. 
Design inference. These are constraints, not 
decorations. Gödel blocks complete self -
grounding of sufficiently expressive formal theo-
ries; Church –Turing blocks a universal effective 
decision procedure; Rice blocks total recognition 
of non-trivial program semantics; Shannon blocks 
the equation of information quantity with epis-
temic standing. The positive architecture is con-
sequently local: declare the horizon, compute only 
decidable or budgeted predicates, return typed 
non-knowledge, preserve receipts, and route au-
thorization outside the evaluator.

CHAPTER 9  
Observer Relativity 
Without Epistemic Rela-
tivism 
Does a declared perspective make every an-
swer equally valid? 
Observer relativity means that representation and 
status are indexed by a declared observer tuple. 
Different horizons may admit different sources, 
languages, queries, tolerances, and authorities. 
The resulting statuses can differ without contra-
diction because the contracts differ. Relativism 
would follow only if no cross -observer compari-
son were possible. ROA instead requires explicit 
comparison of source manifests, query families, 
transmission contracts, validation rules, and gov-
ernance contexts. A disagreement whose contract 
difference can be located is more auditable and 
more open to criticism than an apparently univer-
sal answer whose observer is hidden.

CHAPTER 10  
Evidence States and Typed 
Epistemic Outputs 
What kind of object does the computation re-
turn? 
The core formal object is small. Given a claim and 
a horizon, the function returns one member of a 
finite set of admissible states. The vocabulary may 
be extended by domain, but the principle is fixed: 
the output is an admissibility state, not a truth 
value. This is what makes the term computational 
semantics defensible in a restricted sense — the 
system is not deciding all semantic properties of 
arbitrary programs or worlds; it is deciding wheth-
er a claim satisfies declared proof conditions in a 
bounded ho rizon. The most important result is 
not a state at all, but unpaid warrant recorded be-
side it: a transformation moved meaning in a way 
that touches the claim, but the required receipt or 
validation is missing. The claim may be promising, 
useful, even likely true; what it has earned is rec-
orded, and whether a use is refused is the gate’s

## Page 90

The Accounting Laye r of Computationa l Semantics  
90 
question. This is why a responsible refusal can be 
a successful computation. A confidence score is 
not a proof status: a model can be confident about 
an unsupported claim and uncertain about a sup-
ported but nuanced one. 
The evidence status function is not a truth 
function, and it is not yet a permission either. It 
asks what a claim has earned: raw output, com-
puted but unsupported, supported -not-validated, 
or validated by a check that actually ran. Permis-
sion is the next question and a different function: 
the named-use gate, which alone sees the intended 
use and returns a typed GateOutcome such as 
warranted, permitted -with-waiver, review -
required, horizon-inadequate, or blocked.

Status is therefore dynamic. A claim can move 
from unsupported to supported when a source is 
attached, and from supported to validated when a 
test is run. Warrant is not the next rung: a validat-

an intended use is finally named, and the same

a stronger use is requested. The object did not 
change; the relation between object, horizon and 
use changed. Note the register: once a use is 
named the value is a gate outcome. The evidence 
status stays supported -not-validated in every row; 
the verdict is what moves. 
The rest of the monograph spends these states 
and never again defines them, so they are worth 
one slow pass. Uncomputed is the honest starting 
fact: no one has asked the question under this 
horizon yet. Computed -unsupported is the state 
fluency hides best — the machine produced the 
sentence, and nothing yet stands behind it. Sup-
ported-not-validated marks the first real earning: a 
source is attached and admitted under the hori-

point: no state of the evidence alone can say a 
claim is fit for a purpose, because fitness names a

Around the ladder stand the states that make re-

and not an embarrassment, because incompatible

the debt vector — which the entire accounting 
layer exists to be able to record. The vector does 
not say blocked: blocking is a verdict about a use, 
and neither status nor vector has been told one. 
The set is finite by design and extensible by dec-

clinician — but every extension is itself a declared

What the computation returns, then, is not the 
probability that a sentence is true but the earned 
answer to a narrower question: what this claim, 
under this contract, has paid for. A confidence 
value is a model -side score whose meaning de-
pends on a specified calibration procedure and da-
ta distribution. Evidence status records what 
admitted evidence and declared checks support. 
Neither quantity is truth, and neither by itself au-
thorizes a use. 
Is “I do not know” a phrase, or a computed 
state? 
A conventional system can answer, refuse, or 
say “I do not know.” In a proof environment that 
phrase is not enough: not-knowing must be typed. 
The epistemic head is the component that con-
verts semantic input into an admissible state. It 
need not be a neural head in the machine -learning 
sense; it can be a rule layer, a review protocol, a 
database procedure, a typed workflow, a con-
strained model, or a human-machine checklist.

Four actions matter most. Answer when the sta-
tus allows. Abstain when no support exists. Esca-
late when domain authority or review is required. 
Expose debt when the object is useful but carries 
unpaid warrant. Blocking is the strict case of ex-
posing debt: the debt touches a use that must not 
proceed. This reframes humility: a good system 
does not merely sound cautious; it explains the 
operational reason for its caution and shows what 
evidence would move the claim to a stronger state. 
The head’s placement is the design decision that 
everything else assumes: it sits at the boundary 
where candidate meaning becomes institutional 
act, and the trust boundary sits with it — outside 
the model. The model may draft, summarize, clas-
sify and propose; the head consults objects that are 
governed differently from the model’s output: 
sources, receipts, validation predicates, review 
states. That is why the head can be a rule layer or a 
checklist as easily as a neural component — its au-
thority comes from what it reads, not from what it 
is. 
The epistemic head is the part of the architec-
ture that refuses to collapse every input into an

swer, unknown, contradiction, out -of-horizon 
and review-required — not polite disclaimers but 
terminal states of the computation. Debt -open is 
not among them: it is an annotation that can ac-
company any of them, including answer. 
Epistemic head outputs 
For technical readers, state the head’s relation to 
the gate rather than inferring it: Epistemi-
cHeadOutput = Action x Annotations = ren-
der(evidence_status, debt_vector, gate_outcome). 
It presents rather than decides — invoking the 
gate where a use is named, reporting the evidence 
status where none is. So debt -open means unpaid 
warrant exists, never that a use was refused. The 
head should also not be confused with a confi-
dence threshold. Confidence is a model -side esti-
mate. The epistemic head is a policy -and-evidence 
interface: it presents what the other components 
computed: the evidence status, the debt beside it, 
and where a use is named the gate’s outcome. It 
does not form the judgement; it invokes and ren-
ders it.

Governed differently is a weaker claim than 
immutable, and the weaker claim is the true one. 
Receipts can be model -generated; sources can be

can be authored by the same pipeline they judge; 
review states can be selected to flatter. Six expo-
sures follow — authorship, integrity, freshness, 
revocation, completeness and selection — with 
indicative controls: signing and role separation, 
effective dates, revocation lists, declared source 
manifests, and sampling under an authority the 
requester does not control. Indicative, because 
none is sufficient alone: a signature establishes 
who signed, not that the signer was competent to 
sign. This monograph names the exposures and 
the controls; it does not implement them, and 
Appendix D records the threat -model sketch as a 
TARGET. A trust boundary asserted in a diagram 
is a drawing. What makes it architectural is that 
the objects on the trusted side are the ones an ad-
versary would have to attack in public. 
Abstention deserves its rehabilitation in full. In 
a fluent system, unknown reads as failure; in a 
proof environment it is a successful computation

informative than silence, and actionable, because a 
typed unknown says what would move it: which

review to request. A system that cannot say un-

that can. It has fewer states. 
In this architecture, then, “I do not know” is 
not the system running out of words. It is a termi-
nal state with a type — the computation arriving, 
correctly, at the edge of what the horizon funds, 
and reporting the edge instead of crossing it.

CHAPTER 11  
Scientific Levels as Typed 
Representations 
What is a level when ontology is not as-
sumed? 
RLA begins from a scientific commonplace ra-
ther than a novelty claim: researchers already 
use multiple descriptions, scales, variables, mod-
els, and coarse -grainings. The purpose of the re-
ticular vocabulary is to make the contracts 
among those descriptions explicit and compara-
ble across domains. The scientific burden is 
therefore not to prove that levels exist, but to state 
what each representation can answer, what each 
transmission preserves, and what each collapse 
makes unavailable. 
A level L is a pair <D(L), Sigma(L)>. D(L) is a 
state domain: concentrations, texts, activation 
vectors, transactions, legal propositions, or any 
other declared representation. Sigma(L) is a family 
of admitted operations or dynamics over that do-

## Page 103

The Accounting Laye r of Computationa l Semantics  
103 
main. A level is an epistemic slice of practice, not a 
metaphysical layer of nature. It records the ob-
servables and rules under which a community or 
system performs work. This observer -relative 
treatment follows the model -purpose and scien-
tific-representation tradition rather than asserting 
ontological strata (Giere, 1988; Weisberg, 2013; 
Frigg and Nguyen, 2020; Shalizi and Moore, 
2003). 
Levels are typed. A state in a molecular repre-
sentation cannot be substituted for a population -
level rate without a transmission contract. A label 
cannot be substituted for the evidence that gener-
ated it. This discipline is elementary and decisive: 
many semantic failures are type errors disguised by 
natural language. RLA makes the type boundary 
visible before asking whether the mapping is use-
ful.

Scientific Scope and Falsification Criteria 
RLA does not claim that nature comes pre -
partitioned into levels. It supplies a falsifiable 
bookkeeping grammar: a level or transmission is 
scientifically useful only if its domain, questions, 
preserved distinctions, collapsed distinctions and 
failure conditions can be inspected. An asserted 
cross-level relation fails when a declared query 
cannot be recovered within its tolerance, or when 
the mapping depends on undeclared side infor-
mation. Query -indexed comparison is closest to 
sufficient statistics, Blackwell comparison, infor-
mation bottleneck, abstract interpretation, and 
causal abstraction; RLA claims only the explicit 
coupling of these ideas to typed fibers, receipts, 
and downstream use (Blackwell, 1953; Cousot 
and Cousot, 1977; Tishby, Pereira and Bialek, 
1999; Beckers and Halpern, 2019; Geiger et al., 
2025).

CHAPTER 13  
Collapse, Compression, 
and the Limits of Emer-
gence 
Does non-injectivity create emergence? 
Collapse is a many -to-one map. It can remove dis-
tinctions, reduce cost, stabilize a macro -
description, and enable a new vocabulary. None 
of those consequences is equivalent to emergence. 
A defensible emergence claim must declare micro - 
and macro -languages, encodings, resource 
bounds, admissible algorithms, and invariance 
under reasonable recodings. Relative emergence 
then means that a macro -predicate is computable 
within the macro bound while no admitted micro 
procedure computes its pullback within the micro 
bound. The claim is relative to languages and re-
sources, not absolute non -definability in every 
possible formalism. The boundary is informed by 
renormalization, coarse -graining, computational 
mechanics, and causal -emergence research, all of 
which require stronger structure than mere non -

## Page 113

The Accounting Laye r of Computationa l Semantics  
113 
injectivity (Anderson, 1972; Wilson, 1971; 
Crutchfield and Young, 1989; Shalizi and Crutch-
field, 2001; Rosas et al., 2020; Mediano et al., 
2022). 
This correction matters because the early ROA 
corpus sometimes speaks as though non -injective 
collapse generically guarantees a macro -property 
not definable below. That is too strong without a 
language and resource contract. The revised archi-
tecture retains the insight - collapse can support 
macro-regularity - while replacing the generic the-
orem with a bounded, falsifiable definition. 
Is compression wrong, or only undeclared 
compression? 
Every summary is a collapse. So is every dash-
board, every score, every model level, every execu-
tive one -pager, every traffic -light rating distilled 
from forty pages of findings. The opening chapter 
on representation made peace with this at the level 
of principle — representation is loss, and rightly; 
the chapter on transmissions and query -relative 
fidelity gave it structure — collapse is the non -
injective transmission, the merging of states whose 
distinction carried information. This chapter

## Page 114

The Accounting Laye r of Computationa l Semantics  
114 
prices the everyday case: compression as the ordi-
nary, indispensable, debt-generating act of institu-
tional life. 
Begin with what compression buys, because a 
chapter that only warned would be false to the ar-
gument. Compression makes work possible: no 
board reads every transcript and no engineer holds 
an entire state space. Collapse can make stable 
macro-descriptions and useful regularities availa-
ble at a coarser level, but it does not by itself prove 
that those regularities are emergent, autonomous, 
or unavailable below. The trade is structural and 
cannot be refused, only declared: keep distinctions 
and pay in complexity; merge them and pay in lost 
queries, recovery cost, or downstream debt. 
Collapse debt comes due at one specific mo-

away are needed later but no longer visible. The

Models: Exploratory, Not 
Validated 
Status and Limitations of the Original Retic-
ular Metrics 
The source corpus proposed a coefficient of col-
lapse, an emergence index, and a reticular irreduc-
ibility index. These are retained as exploratory 
diagnostics, not validated measurement scales. A 
publishable metric must specify its scale type, in-
variances, estimator, error model, calibration data, 
and decision relevance. Until those obligations are 
met, the three indices may rank examples inside a 
frozen toy model but may not be compared across 
domains or cited as evidence of emergence. Their 
falsifier is straightforward: if independent coders 
or perturbation tests show that the ranking 
changes under representation choices that should 
be immaterial, the metric lacks construct validity.

What should be measured before a reticulum 
is trusted? 
Useful diagnostics include fiber cardinality or en-
tropy, distortion on declared query families, colli-
sion rates, contradiction rates, abstention 
coverage, dependency completeness, and the cost 
of reconstructing a source path. These are not one 
scalar. A transmission can have low geometric dis-
tortion and high authority debt; an epistemic head 
can be well calibrated and poorly sourced. ROA 
therefore treats metrics as a vector indexed by lay-
er and intended use. 
Fiber distortion.  How much can a declared 
query vary inside one fiber? This measures query -
relevant loss rather than generic compression. 
Collision profile.  Which distinctions are 
merged, at which transmission, and for which lat-
er uses do those collisions matter? 
Decoder success. Can a declared query value—
or, where required, a source state —be recon-
structed from the target representation under the 
stated decoder contract?

horizon. The broader research programme is 
constructive rather than foundational: ask 
whether enough of a scientific model can be com-

imations become inspectable.

CRC becomes scientifically interesting only when 
it is forced to compile something that resists clean 
closure. The bryophyte case does that work. The 
source model assembles twenty abstraction levels 
and forty -two parameters from plant physiology 
and ecology, with update equations, causal rela-
tions, scenarios, thresholds, and a finite execution 
loop. That construction witnesses that a litera-
ture-derived reticulum can be made explicit and 
executable; it does not establish that the plant has 
been reproduced, that every parameter is identifi-
able, or that the selected literature is complete. 
The important event is what happens at the 
seams. Scientific literature does not arrive as one 
interoperable program. A needed relation may be 
species-specific and directly measured; it may be 
reported only as a range; it may be known qualita-
tively but not as a calibrated function; it may have 
to cross taxon or scale; or it may be absent. A 
compiler - human or AI -assisted - must therefore

Epistemic Computational 
Units as Local Semantic 
Operators 
Epistemic Matrices, Deterministic Regimes, 
and Self-Audit 
The ECU specification used the term epistemic 
matrix for the local schema of admissible inputs, 
transformations, terminal states, evidence re-
quirements, and authority constraints. In this 
monograph the matrix is not a learned truth table; 
it is a versioned policy and type object. “Deter-
ministic ECU regime” now refers only to the cer-
tified control plane: fixed input hashes, versioned 
operators, fixed scheduler, schema validation, pol-
icy evaluation, and receipt construction. A genera-
tive model call remains a candidate-producing 
operation unless bit -level replay has actually been 
established; temperature zero, a fixed seed, or a 
named checkpoint is not treated as a proof of de-
terministic output, and empirical nondetermin-
ism is recorded rather than defined away

## Page 147

The Accounting Laye r of Computationa l Semantics  
147 
(Summers and Dinneen, 2021). Self -audit means 
replaying the unit against declared invariants, re-
ceipts, and challenge suites; it does not grant the 
unit authority to certify itself. 
What is the smallest governed semantic 
transducer? 
An Epistemic Computational Unit (ECU, or 
UCE in Italian) is a typed partial transducer. It 
consumes a local value, horizon fragment, evi-
dence state, policy state, and resource budget; it 
emits a typed value plus an immutable receipt, or 
one of the declared terminal constructors. The 
unit is local: it does not own the global truth of 
the reticulum. Its contract states input and output 
types, admitted transformations, validation predi-
cates, failure modes, and which evidence or debt 
components it may change. Its inherited formal 
neighbours are labelled transition systems, partial 
transducers, typed effects, provenance, and assur-
ance arguments; the proposed delta is the receipt -
bearing epistemic contract and its non -answer 
terminals (Plotkin, 1981; Belnap, 1977; W3C, 
2013a–c; Bishop and Bloomfield, 1998).

## Page 148

The Accounting Laye r of Computationa l Semantics  
148 
This design separates model computation from 
epistemic standing. A language model may be an 
operator inside an ECU, but the ECU does not 
derive authority from the model. It derives its 
standing from the contract and the external ob-
jects it reads: source manifests, receipts, valida-
tions, policies, and review states. The unit is 
therefore implementable as a function, service, 
workflow, rule engine, checklist, or human -
machine step.

Is an ECNN necessarily a neural network? 
An ECNN is a typed reticulum of ECUs, repre-
sentation operators, a scheduler, an epistemic 
head, and an explicit state register. Early docu-
ments use a CNN analogy: convolution supplies 
local receptive fields, pooling supplies collapse, 
and an epistemic layer supplies unknown and 
contradiction. That analogy is historical and non -
constitutive. The mature object is a deterministic 
navigation and validation substrate over a seman-
tic reticulum whose nodes may be human -
certified, AI -candidate, disputed, superseded , un-
known, or contradictory. Neural models can pro-
pose nodes, links, labels, and summaries; they do 
not acquire certification authority by being inside 
the graph. Selective prediction, conformal risk

an epistemic network cannot be validated by clas-

outputs include abstention, contradiction, and 
review routing.

The logical movement is progressive. At level 0,

certified and candidate objects remain jointly nav-

therefore grow while preserving the difference be-
tween what a machine suggested and what an ac-
countable person signed.

BRIDGE — THE FRAMEWORK APPLIED 
TO ITSELF 
Selective prediction provides a formal ancestor 
for abstention: the system trades coverage for low-
er risk (Chow, 1970; El -Yaniv and Wiener, 2010; 
Geifman and El -Yaniv, 2017). ROA adds two di-
mensions. First, the reason for abstention is typed: 
insufficient evidence, contradiction, horizon fail-
ure, authority, resource exhaustion, or an unde-
cidable promise problem. Second, the terminal 
travels with a receipt describing what would 
change it. This is not a claim that all uncertainty 
can be resolved into a finite taxonomy. It is a claim 
that the system must not collapse every unresolved 
condition into an answer token.

Modal Hygiene, Epistemic History, and Met-

Modal hygiene is the rule that constructible, ob-
served, supported, warranted, and necessary 
claims remain different types. The observer com-
piler therefore persists an epistemic history: a ver-
sioned sequence of horizons, inputs, 
transformations, terminals, reviews, waivers, and 
revocations. Path dependence is operational when 
two identical current inputs can legitimately yield 
different outcomes because their histories contain 
different receipts, authority states, or unresolved 
contradictions. Metacognitive monitoring is used 
only in this engineering sense: the system measures 
its own resource state, coverage, conflicts, and pol-
icy triggers. It is neither phenomenal awareness 
nor privileged self-knowledge.

How is a field turned into a governed reticu-
lum? 
Observer compilation is the construction process 
that turns a bounded field into an explicit observ-
er. The compiler identifies source classes, levels, 
state types, query families, transmissions, local op-
erators, receipts, validation predicates, terminal 
states, and governance routes. It emits not only an 
executable graph but also a source manifest, type 
environment, invariant registry, claim -to-evidence 
map, failure policy, and rollback plan. The com-
piler is itself inside the audit horizon: its prompts, 
transformations, and human interventions are 
candidate artefacts, not invisible authorship. The 
selected established comparators are assurance 
cases, runtime monitors, provenance systems, 
knowledge representation, and end -to-end system 
contracts; ROA must outperform or clarify these 
neighbours rather than merely rename them 
(Bishop and Bloomfield, 1998; Bloomfield and 
Bishop, 2010; Saltzer, Reed and Clark, 1984; 
W3C, 2013a–c; Fagin et al., 1995). 
The central move is to treat intermediate arte-
facts as first-class. Definitions, taxonomies, formu-

## Page 162

The Accounting Laye r of Computationa l Semantics  
162 
las, issue chains, graph fragments, and review 
notes are persisted and linked rather than discard-
ed after a final answer. Cumulative intelligence 
then resides in the governed substrate and the 
human decisions that shape it, not in one transi-
ent model call. This is the difference between nav-
igating knowledge and repeatedly improvising it. 
What is gained by navigation over generation? 
A governed oracle is not an omniscient oracle. It 
is a responder over a bounded reticulum. Given a 
query, it traverses typed relations, evaluates evi-
dence and debt, invokes relevant ECUs, and re-
turns a terminal plus a reconstructable path. Its 
distinctive value is persistence: the same source, 
receipt, transformation, and human decision can 
support later queries without being recreated. Its 
distinctive restraint is typed non -knowledge: 
when no admissible path supports a use, the re-
sponse is unknown, contradiction, review, or out -
of-horizon rather than invented closure. 
Navigation does not eliminate generation. 
Models can still propose queries, candidate links, 
summaries, and hypotheses. The architecture 
changes their role. Generated material is a candi-

authenticating evidence. The model becomes a 
replaceable operator over a durable semantic field.

Execution Does Not Establish Legitimacy 
A ROA can enforce a versioned normative kernel 
and prove that a run conformed to it. It cannot 
infer from conformance that the kernel was mor-
ally, legally, or democratically legitimate. Issuing 
authority, contestation, affected -party review, ef-
fective dates, and revocation are therefore external 
governance premises carried in the observer con-
tract. This separation is essential for philosophers 
of science and engineers alike: an executable norm 
is a fact about a system; a justified norm is a claim 
in a social and legal order. 
Falsifier of overclaim. Construct two internally 
consistent kernels with incompatible prescrip-
tions. Execution alone cannot choose which is le-
gitimate without importing an authority 
relation not derived from the runtime.

CHAPTER 24  
Controlled Reification: 
When Patterns Become 
Objects 
When does a pattern become a dangerous ob-
ject? 
Reification is the promotion of a pattern, label, 
relation or abstraction into a manipulable object. 
In ordinary work this happens constantly: a re-
peated payment practice becomes a control, a 
cluster of symptoms becomes a case flag, a recur-
ring code smell becomes a technical -debt issue, a 
narrative motif becomes a character trait. Reifica-
tion is not wrong — knowledge advances by mak-
ing objects that can be inspected, tested and 
reused. 
The danger is uncontrolled reification: when a 
candidate object is treated as validated, when the 
conditions of its construction disappear, or when 
downstream systems rely on it without knowing 
its status. Controlled reification keeps the promo-
tion traceable, status -bearing and reversible: it

## Page 176

The Accounting Laye r of Computationa l Semantics  
176 
records the source pattern, the operator, the new 
object, the distinctions lost, the status carried, the 
allowed and refused uses, and a rollback or dis-
charge path. 
Controlled reification means that the system is 
allowed to promote a sentence into an object only 
if the promotion carries its papers. The CFO sen-
tence may become a control object, but it must 
carry its source, scope, extraction method, review 
state and allowed uses. Without those fields, the 
object becomes easier to reuse precisely because it 
has become harder to challenge. 
Controlled reification is also a permission to 
work. The monograph is not asking institutions 
to stop naming things. It is asking them to name 
things with enough metadata that the name re-
mains revisable. A provisional object is useful pre-
cisely because it can be reused without pretending 
to be final.

CHAPTER 25  
Epistemic Debt: The Un-
paid Remainder of Seman-
tic Transformation 
Is debt the same as being wrong? 
Epistemic Debt is the unresolved warrant left by a 
semantic transformation and carried by the result-
ing object whether or not a use has yet been 
named. A debt-bearing object is not automatically 
false and not automatically useless. Its vector rec-
ords source, trace, transformation, collapse, label, 
reification, validation, authority, and horizon -or-
scale obligations under the current horizon; a later 
gate determines whether those obligations are tol-
erable, review -requiring, or blocking for a named 
use. A draft risk factor may therefore be usable for 
brainstorming and blocked for board reporting 
without its debt severity changing. The asset side 
records what was conserved and supported: 
source, scope, receipt, readback, validation, re-
viewer authority. The liability side records what

## Page 178

The Accounting Laye r of Computationa l Semantics  
178 
was lost or remains unjustified: missing source, 
unvalidated inference, overbroad label, scale trans-
fer, modality drift, or premature reification. A 
transformation is honest when both sides are 
booked; it becomes dangerous when only the asset 
side is shown. A hallucination is a severe special 
case—a debt falsely presented as paid —but the 
theory also covers silent gaps and valid claims used 
outside their horizon. The claimed delta is a typed, 
componentwise, use -independent liability com-
bined with a separate use -sensitive gate (Cun-
ningham, 1992; Kruchten, Nord and Ozkaya, 
2012; Sculley et al., 2015; IAASB, 2018; Moreau 
and Groth, 2013). 
The liability is institutional because down-
stream users often meet only the polished object, 
not the missing warrant. A dashboard tile, a legal 
issue list, a scientific variable or a product risk 
score can all borrow authority from presentation. 
The ledger counters this by making the liability 
travel with the object until discharged, or until a 
gate logs a waiver for a named use.

CHAPTER 26  
The Debt Vector: Why 
One Score Is Not Enough 
Why is one red flag not enough? 
Debt is not one thing. A claim can be well sourced 
but poorly scoped, well scoped but unvalidated, 
validated in one domain but transferred to anoth-
er, or supported as a possibility but written as a 
certainty. A single red flag hides these distinctions; 
a vector preserves them. The proposed nine -
component vector is a candidate coding instru-
ment, not yet a validated or universal metric. Its 
ontology is part of the research hypothesis until 
independent componentwise reliability and in-
cremental utility over sim pler prove-
nance/missing-data baselines are established. Its 
nine components are source, trace, transfor-
mation, collapse, label, reification, validation, au-
thority, and horizon -or-scale debt. Each 
component should be coded with examples, 
thresholds and discharge conditions, so a reviewer 
can say not only that a claim is risky but why —

## Page 182

The Accounting Laye r of Computationa l Semantics  
182 
missing source, broken trace, invalid label, unre-
viewed authority, unsupported transfer, or over-
compressed summary. Different debts demand 
different remedies, and the same total risk can 
hide very different repair paths. The vector also 
disciplines performative caution: “needs review” is 
too vague; the vector says which review, which 
dependency, which missing receipt, and which use 
is blocked until the problem is paid.

The vector is learned by use rather than by list, 
and each component carries its own diagnostic 
question. Source debt asks the oldest question: 
can the origin be identified and admitted under 
the horizon? A board memo resting on “internal 
analysis” that no one can produce is not wrong 
yet; it is unpayable, which is worse. Trace debt 
asks whether the path from source to claim can be 
reconstructed. A true claim with a broken trace is 
a liability in a fact’s clothes: it survives every chal-
lenge except the first serious one. 
Transformation debt asks whether meaning was 
changed by a declared, allowed operation. Sum-
maries, translations, extractions and classifications 
all move meaning; undocumented movement is 
debt even when the destination happens to be 
right, because rightness can no longer be shown. 
Collapse debt asks whether distinctions were 
compressed away that a later use will need — the 
dashboard question, priced in full in the chapter 
on information collapse, compression, and emer-
gence. Label debt asks whether the name e xceeds 
its criteria: the five letters of “fixed” on a sandbox -

## Page 185

The Accounting Laye r of Computationa l Semantics  
185 
tested patch; the two words “control exists” over a 
partial practice in two departments. 
Reification debt asks whether a candidate was 
promoted early — an object minted before its pa-
pers, easier to reuse precisely because it is harder to 
challenge. Validation debt asks the bluntest ques-
tion in the set: has the required check actually 
run? Not “is it plausible”, not “does it read well” 
— did the sample get drawn, did the test execute, 
did it pass. Authority debt asks which authority is 
documented for the reviewer or source; the gate 
compares it with what a use requires. A brilliant 
unauthorized reading is still unauthorized, and in 
law, audit and medicine this component alone can 
decide the gate. Horizon-or-scale debt asks wheth-
er warrant earned in one place is being spent in 
another: one interview billed as a population, a lab 
constant billed as a field prediction, last year’s 
scope billed as this year’s. 
Nine, and deliberately not one, because the 
components fail independently and the remedies 
do not transfer: a missing source is paid at a differ-
ent counter than an overreaching label, and a vali-
dation gap cannot be discharged by a signature —

The Accounting Laye r of Computationa l Semantics

only postponed by one. This is also why the vec-
tor resists collapsing into a single score: the pool-

makes the debt payable — which counter. When a 
single decision is nonetheless required, the named-

CHAPTER 27  
Proof Chains and Use 
Gates: Discharge, Waiver, 
and Authorization 
What turns an output into something an in-
stitution may rely on? 
Within this architecture, an output becomes insti-
tutionally usable only by crossing the declared 
proof chain. A source becomes an atom; an atom 
receives a receipt; a receipt supports an artefact; an 
artefact becomes a witness; a witness enters gov-
ernance. These transitions are proof -relevant 
boundaries: some transform or validate evidence, 
while only the final named -use gate determines 
permission. A generated paragraph is not proof, a 
log is not automatically a receipt, an export is not 
automatically a witness, a green interface is not 
automatically warrant, and model memory is not 
an epistemic authority. These false equivalences 
are common ways debt launders into authority. 
A proof chain keeps the trust boundary outside 
the proposing model. The model may transform,

## Page 190

The Accounting Laye r of Computationa l Semantics  
190 
summarize, classify, or propose; the governed evi-
dence substrate consists of inspectable sources, 
receipts, readback, validation predicates, depend-
ency records, and authorization events. Those ob-
jects can still be incomplete, stale, forged, or 
institutionally illegitimate, so the architecture 
treats them as reviewable evidence rather than 
truth. The proof chain extends provenance and 
assurance-case disciplines by making evidence sta-
tus, residual debt, named use, and waiver or dis-
charge state explicit rather than treating lineage 
itself as permission (Buneman, Khanna and Tan, 
2001; Cheney, Chiticariu and Tan, 2009; W3C, 
2013a–c; Kelly and Weaver, 2004; Necula, 1997). 
The chain should be simple enough for humans 
to inspect and strict enough for machines to en-
force. Its positive side is proof capital: a source at-
om with scope, receipt, readback, validation and 
witness can serve many later registers — audit, le-
gal review, compliance, environmental -social-
governance review, and scientific provenance — 
so the ledger is not only a brake but a memory sys-
tem for earned warrant.

A proof chain is a chain of typed, proof -bearing 
transformations that culminates in a named -use 
decision. Earlier links establish source, transfor-
mation, validation, or review facts; only the gate 
grants or refuses standing for the intended use. 
Minimal proof-chain object 
Linear and reticular reading: the chain is linear 
when a single claim travels from source to deci-
sion. It becomes reticular when several claims 
share sources, receipts, transformations or govern-
ance decisions. That reticular reuse is proof capi-
tal, but only if each reuse preserves the status 
boundary of the original object. 
When is conditional use legitimate? 
A gate compares proof status and debt against 
an intended use. The same object can pass a brain-
storming gate, fail a board -reporting gate, and re-
quire a waiver for a deadline -sensitive preliminary 
use. That is not inconsistency; it is use -sensitive 
governance. Thresholds should be explicit: some 
debts are tolerable for low -risk exploration, some 
require review, and some block authoritative use. 
Authority debt is especially delicate: a model may 
propose a legal, medical, safety, or audit claim, but

fused. Discharge pays a specified debt component 
only when the new event is admissible for that 
component and scope: evidence may pay source 
debt, a completed check may pay validation debt, 
contradiction resolution may pay a contradiction -
related obligation, and an authorized review may 
pay authority or validation debt only where the

evidence. A signature cannot discharge unrelated

Waiver does not pay; it records a bounded deci-

reason, owner, expiry, and residual risk. 
A gate is where the ledger stops being descrip-
tive and becomes operational. A gate does not ask 
whether a claim sounds plausible. It asks whether 
the intended use is allowed under current status. 
If not, the path branches: discharge the debt, log a 
waiver with owner and expiry, narrow the use, or 
block the downstream action.

debt by adding evidence or review. A waiver per-

CHAPTER 28  
Anti-False-Green: Pre-
venting Unsupported Suc-
cess 
Can the system fail honestly? 
The non -laundering invariant is simple: no unre-
solved threshold-level debt may become authorita-
tive use without discharge or logged waiver. It is 
not mathematically deep; its importance is archi-
tectural. It prevents a system from converting un-
knowns, gaps and unverified transformations into 
institutional certainty by style, formatting or 
workflow convenience. 
False green is the interface version of launder-
ing: a modal says complete, a dashboard turns 
green, an issue is closed, a document is exported, 
or a model emits confident prose, but the proof 
predicates have not passed. It is dangerous because 
it creates the social appearance of payment with-
out the epistemic payment. Anti -false-green de-
sign therefore requires negative tests — the system 
must demonstrate that it refuses green when a re-

## Page 196

The Accounting Laye r of Computationa l Semantics  
196 
ceipt is missing, when readback fails, when scope 
is absent, or when a critical debt touches the in-
tended use. A proof -sensitive system should be 
willing to block itself for the right reason. 
False green is the system -level form of epistemic 
laundering. It occurs when an interface, export, 
log, confidence score, or waiver is presented as if it 
were warranted use without the receipts and re-
view state that would justify that status. The anti -
false-green rule is strict: warranted green may be 
derived only from a current WARRANTED gate 
outcome and its receipts.  
PERMITTED_WITH_WAIVER is a distinct, 
visibly qualified state carrying residual debt, own-
er, scope, reason, and expiry; it may permit action 
but must never visually or semantically masquer-
ade as warrant. 
The practical test is adversarial. A mature sys-
tem should include negative tests that deliberately 
remove receipt, readback, source or reviewer state 
and verify that the interface cannot still present an 
authoritative green. Anti -false-green is a property 
of failure behavior, not of the happy path.

What travels by necessity, what travels by 
dependency, and what changes by choice? 
The preceding sections built the ledger: a claim 
has status only under a horizon; a reification cre-
ates an object; debt is unpaid warrant; a gate pre-
vents unresolved debt from becoming authority. 
Part VII asks a different question: once a debt or 
limit exists, how does it move? The answer is not 
one mechanism but three, and confusing them is 
one of the fastest ways to overclaim the theory. 
Some things travel by necessity. Where a critical 
channel is preserved, a formal limit at one level in-
duces a formal limit at another. No review, signa-
ture or governance ritual pays this kind of 
No. The only honest action is to expose the limit, 
change the channel, or narrow the question. This 
is the formal side of propagation and it is the part 
that remains owed as a stronger theorem wherever

One term must be paid for locally, because the 
whole necessary tier hangs on it. A channel is criti-

tion turns on survive transmission across it — 
when answering upstairs still requires telling apart 
states the channel keeps apart. Keep the distinc-
tions and the limit below rides through with 
them; merge them and the question upstairs is not 
answered but blocked — a different fate with a 
different price, and the chapter on information 
collapse, compression, and emergence keeps its 
price sheet. 
In miniature: whether one specific payment was

cannot even be asked. The aggregate solved noth-

injective transformation can block a formal ques-

macro-regularities and usable abstractions. But a 
collapse is not amnesty. It is a price sheet: if the 
lost distinctions are needed later, the debt returns. 
The chapter on information collapse, compres-
sion, and emergence gives the everyday accounting 
of that price. The practical rule is simple: name 
the kind of travel before choosing the remedy.

When is similarity not inheritance of war-

The third traveller. The preceding chapter’s limits

object from the horizon where it earned its stand-

among the easiest ways to create hidden debt, pre-
cisely because it feels like the opposite: reuse reads 
as thrift, analogy reads as insight, and the object 
arrives with its old confidence still attached, like 
furniture shipped with the tags of the previous 
house.

transfer moves the object but not the warrant, be-
cause warrant was never a property of the object

Move it, and the assumptions that funded the 
warrant may quietly fail in the target: the related

compresses; the neighbouring jurisdiction shares

Nothing about the object changed. Everything 
about its backing did — and similarity of surface 
is precisely what hides it, because similarity is a 
claim about the objects, and warrant was never 
about the objects. 
The special case with its own name is scale -
transfer debt: warrant earned at one scale, spent at 
another. One interview supports an observation; 
it does not support a population claim — the 
sample was sized for the first sentence and is being 
billed for the second. A lab model supports a 
mechanism; it does not support field behaviour — 
the controls that made the mechanism visible are

on credit, and the drift between them is usually

Reticular Warrant Struc-
ture 
How can AI help science without pretending 
to be science? 
Science is the hardest register for a book like this 
to enter without overclaiming, and so the entry is 
made under a strict rule, stated first: the observer 
is not a knower of the world; it is a governed 
structure for making the status of representations 
explicit. With that stake in the ground, the ques-
tion becomes answerable. AI can help science not 
by doing science — not by paying the empirical 
debt only experiment can pay — but by compil-
ing it: reading a domain reticularly, as levels, vari-
ables, equation s, parameter ranges, validation 
criteria, failure modes and admitted sources, and 
making that structure computable, inspectable 
and falsifiable. The warrant stays human, empiri-
cal, revisable and domain -bound. What the ob-

## Page 221

The Accounting Laye r of Computationa l Semantics  
221 
server adds is not knowledge but bookkeeping of 
obligation. 
Read this way, a scientific corpus becomes a 
governed evidence node: a bounded set of pub-
lished claims, models, parameters, and validation 
obligations compiled into the observer’s horizon. 
It is an evidence and model substrate rather than 
an epistemic authority, and it does not replace the 
field  
it represents. Compiling it makes debts visible 
that fluent synthesis hides: literature -selection 
debt; parameter -harmonisation debt; equation -
transfer debt; scale debt; model -closure debt; and 
empirical-validation debt, which only observation 
or experiment can discharge. 
Everything in this chapter turns on one distinc-
tion, and it is the distinction most often lost pre-
cisely where it matters most: computability is not 
validation. A model can be internally computable 
— it runs, it terminates, it produces coherent, 
even beautiful outputs — and remain entirely un-
validated for the scientific purpose that matters. A 
simulation that halts is not a simulation that is 
true. The peril is that mathematical elegance reads

## Page 222

The Accounting Laye r of Computationa l Semantics

as warrant: a clean model, a smooth curve, an 
equation that closes, all wear the appearance of 
having earned something they have not. The ob-
server’s contribution is to keep that gap from be-
ing papered over by the aesthetics of the 
formalism — to hold, beside every computed tra-
jectory, the open ledger of what it still owes the 
world. Put positively, and this is the sentence the 
chapter exists to deliver: a compiled reticulum 
does not answer the scientific question; it tells the 
experiment where to bite — it locates, precisely, 
the parameter that most needs measuring, the 
transfer that most needs testing, the closure that 
most needs relaxing. The observer is not a rival to 
the laboratory. It is the laboratory’s map of its 
own most valuable ignorance. 
So — how can AI help science without pretend-
ing to be science? By compiling its claims and ob-
ligations into a governed, falsifiable structure and 
then stopping — leaving the warrant exactly 
where it belongs, with evidence, with expertise, 
with the world — so that the machine’s real gift to 
science is not an answer but a sharpened question, 
and the honesty to keep the two apart.

and not a live-coupled engineering digital twin. Its

until compared with observations under an exter-

The right claim is deliberately modest. The re-

those trajectories can in principle be compared 
with empirical observations or blind expert

indistinguishability: under a fixed set of observa-

This is a target, not a result. It is scientifically in-
formative only if the observables and threshold are 
fixed before inspection, trivial baselines are in-
cluded, experts are appropriately sampled, and 
failure modes such as mode collapse, data leakage, 
and selective reporting are tested. A favourable 
result on one observable family would not estab-
lish biological equivalence or validity outside that 
family. 
The gloss is a warning against two seductions: a 
reticulum is not true because the literature was 
mined, and not valid because a machine helped 
organise it. Neither the provenance of the inputs 
nor the sophistication of the assembly discharges 
empirical debt. The model’s warrant depends on 
source quality, honest parameter reconciliation, 
explicit equations, expert review, and empirical 
discrimination against the world. Its value is not 
that it might be indistinguishable by construction;

explicit and testable, converting “the literature

wager of the case: not a moss to believe, but a

review. An auditor who has never heard the word

tested. The ledger does not teach compliance a 
new morality. It gives an existing morality a type 
system — and that is why compliance is the 
wedge: the least translation, the fastest recogni-
tion, the shortest distance between this mono-
graph’s vocabulary and a working desk.

Does the ledger generalize, or impose one for-
mula on every domain?

A framework that fit only compliance and sci-

chapter tests the ledger’s reach by turning it on 
three worlds that price warrant in visibly different 
currencies — and the finding is the one the mon-
ograph needs: the structure generalises; the mean-
ing of warrant is local, and stays local. The ledger 
supplies the common grammar — source, scope, 
transformation, receipt, review, use — and each 
register fills that grammar with its own evidence 
and its own authority. The lawyer still decides le-
gal adequacy; the engineer, release readiness; the 
scientist, validation; the author, canon. The ledger 
does not annex expertise. It gives experts of every 
kind a shared way to say what stands behind this, 
and for what use — and then gets out of the way. 
Walk the three, and watch the same six -station 
chain speak three languages. In software, warrant 
comes from tests, review, runtime evidence, secu-
rity checks and rollback paths; a receipt is a pass-
ing CI run with a readback of what was actually 
deployed, and false green has a literal cousin — 
the pipeline that reports success while a check was 
skipped. In law, warrant comes from jurisdiction,

posture; a source atom is a statute or a holding, 
and authority debt is not a nuance but the whole

however fluent, and the eighth component of the 
vector governs the register. In creative work, war-
rant shifts register entirely and does not thereby 
vanish: it may mean internal coherence, declared 
draft status, attribution, or consistency with an 
established canon; a “fact” about a fictional world 
is warranted by the author’s acceptance, and a 
generated lore summary is a draft until the pen 
that owns the world says otherwise. That these are 
so different is the point: warrant is not one thing 
wearing four hats; it is four things sharing one 
skeleton. 
One caution closes the chapter, aimed at a fail-
ure the framework could commit rather than one 
it detects. The ledger’s generality is a genuine asset 
and a standing temptation: because the grammar 
fits everywhere, it can be imposed everywhere, 
flattening the expert judgement it was meant to 
serve — a compliance -shaped template stamped 
onto a poem, a software gate bolted onto a diag-

The generality of the ledger depends on localiz-

tests, review and deployment evidence. In law, it

What Would Count as 
Empirical Improvement? 
What would show that the ledger changes 
real work? 
The theory becomes stronger when it says how it 
could be wrong. If a debt ledger does not improve 
detection of unsupported use, reduce false green, 
cut reconstruction time, improve reviewer agree-
ment, or improve downstream decisions, then its 
practical value is weaker than claimed. Hallucina-
tion rate is relevant but insufficient as the primary 
metric: a system can avoid lexical hallucination 
while still producing unsupported authoritative 
use, and it can produce a factually wrong but 
properly blocked candidate without creating an 
authorized failure. The primary endpoint there-
fore targets the event the architecture claims to 
prevent: unsupported authoritative use under a 
declared horizon and governance contract. 
Hallucination rate deserves one more sentence 
of demotion, because it is the metric everyone
