tion to zero and launder happily: every sentence 
sourced, every source real, and the whole assem-
bled into an authority the evidence never earned. 
Conversely, a workflow can hallucinate occasion-
ally and stay honest, if the ledger catches the fabri-
cation before use. The target variable was never 
falsehood in the output; it is unsupported author-
ity in the use — and only the second is what insti-
tutions actually pay for. 
A publication -ready ledger therefore carries its 
own readiness states: implemented, witnessed, tar-
get, open, and not -a-claim. These states do not 
make the work weaker. They make the strongest 
claims easier to see because they prevent every 
weaker claim from being silently promoted. 
Measurement begins with separation. A study 
should not ask whether the framework is “good” 
in the abstract. It should ask whether typed hori-
zons, receipts and debt gates reduce specific failure 
modes: unsupported downstream use, reconstruc-
tion time, false -green events, unreviewed authori-
ty upgrades and hidden waivers.

Differential Contribution 
Against Selected Research 
Traditions 
Which established traditions already solve 
parts of the problem? 
Scientific representations are selective and pur-
pose-relative rather than literal duplicates of their 
targets (Giere, 1988; Hacking, 1983; Frigg & 
Nguyen, 2020; Weisberg, 2013). Information 
theory and information -flow semantics distin-
guish message capacity from meaning and distrib-
uted constraint (Shannon, 1948; Barwise & 
Seligman, 1997; Floridi, 2011). Abstract interpre-
tation gives sound approximation relations be-
tween concrete and abstract program domains 
(Cousot & Cousot, 1977). Blackwell comparison 
orders experiments by decision -relevant informa-
tiveness (Blackwell, 1953), information bottleneck 
methods preserve predictive relevance under 
compression (Tishby et al., 1999), and causal ab-

straction studies when low - and high -level causal 
models agree under interventions (Pearl, 2009; 
Rubenstein et al., 2017; Beckers & Halpern, 2019; 
Beckers et al., 2020). Work on emergence, coarse -
graining, and universality also shows that macro -
level usefulness, critical behavior, and computa-
tional simulation require stronger premises than 
many-to-one encoding (Anderson, 1972; Wilson, 
1971; Batterman, 2002; Humphreys, 2016; Wolf-
ram, 1984, 2002; Cook, 2004). These traditions 
justify query - or intervention -relative fidelity. 
They do not determine whether a produced se-
mantic object has adequate evidence, governance 
authority, or a valid downstream use. 
Database provenance distinguishes why -, 
where-, and how -provenance and supplies formal 
derivation semantics (Buneman et al., 2001; 
Cheney et al., 2009; Moreau & Groth, 2013). 
W3C PROV standardizes entities, activities, and 
agents (W3C, 2013a, 2013b). Reproducible re-
search requires executable methods, inspectable 
data, and rerunnable artifacts (Donoho, 2010; 
Nosek et al., 2015; Munafò et al., 2017). Distrib-
uted-systems design further distinguishes an

Selective classification formalizes reject options

abstention. None turns confidence into prove-

What is the narrowest defensible contribution? 
No individual ingredient is new. The contribu-
tion is a typed composition in which query fideli-
ty, evidence, debt, reification, and use authority 
retain separate semantics while participating in 
one artifact and one decision procedure. The 
strongest mathematical contribution is the use of 
factorization and recoverability as the exact mean-
ing of purpose-relative preservation. The strongest 
architectural contribution is a trace safety invari-
ant with explicit trusted assumptions. The strong-
est methodological contribution is to make 
operational superiority falsifiable against simpler 
baselines.

CHAPTER 38  
Open Scientific Debt and 
Conditions of Defeat 
What must be true outside the formal core 
before ROA earns scientific or operational 
standing? 
The indexed formal statements are heterogeneous 
and premise -sensitive. Their premises define a 
trusted computational envelope; they do not cer-
tify sources, policies, monitors, institutions or the 
external world. A severe review must therefore dis-
tinguish proof inside the calculus from validity of 
the calculus for a deployment. ROA fails scientifi-
cally if it hides that bridge. 
Internal validity is threatened when a theorem 
encodes the desired conclusion in a transition rule, 
mediation premise, or monitor assumption. The 
by-construction safety results F12 –F14 and the 
terminal-preservation result F24 are useful con-
formance guarantees, but they are not independ-
ent evidence that a policy is adequate, that 
dependencies are complete, or that every real use

## Page 271

The Accounting Laye r of Computationa l Semantics  
271 
surface is mediated. Construct validity is threat-
ened when query fidelity, evidence status, debt, 
confidence, and truth are measured by one proxy. 
External validity is threatened when a reticulum, 
threshold, or debt ontology is moved across do-
mains without a transfer passport and local valida-
tion. 
Provenance completeness is the central infor-
mation-science risk: debt propagates only along 
recorded or discoverable dependencies. Security is 
the central systems risk: an unmonitored bypass 
can invalidate the non-laundering guarantee while 
leaving the internal trace perfectly safe. Human 
governance is the central institutional risk: a 
transparent waiver can still be illegitimate, coer-
cive or systematically biased. Performance and 
adoption are the central engineering risks: a sys-
tem that is formally honest but too costly or cum-
bersome may be bypassed in practice. 
A conforming implementation must therefore 
ship more than code. It requires a versioned sche-
ma, a reference interpreter or executable seman-
tics, a frozen conformance corpus, positive and 
negative tests, a threat model, monitored use sur-

Severe-review verdict. 
The ROA/Epistemic Debt architecture is for-
mally coherent relative to its declared signatures 
and assumptions, but its scientific standing re-
mains conditional on public conformance arte-
facts, independent mathematical review, and 
empirical evaluation. This monograph is therefore 
releasable as a theoretical and formal -
methodological research monograph, not as evi-
dence of empirical superiority, production assur-
ance, calibrated governance, or universal observer 
completeness.

The debt ontology may be too coarse, too fine, 
or domain -dependent. Ordinal scales may not 
support stable coding. The evidence -status rules 
can be poor even when applied consistently. Ap-
pend-only lineage can conflict with privacy, eras-

What does a running system prove — and 
what can it never prove? 
A theory of warrant that never touched a running 
system would be right to be suspicious of itself. 
But a theory that pointed at a running system and 
said “see, it works, therefore the theory is true” 
would be committing, in public and at the very 
end, the exact fallacy the preceding sections 
named. This chapter walks the narrow path be-
tween those two failures. The source corpus con-
tains a reference build — an append -only, text -
first, browser -native environment for AI -assisted 
work — and the whole task here is to say, with the 
monograph’s own discipline turned inward, pre-
cisely what that build does and does not entitle the 
monograph to claim. 
The mechanism is one exact distinction: a run-
ning implementation can witness constructibility 
of a specified mechanism, but it does not establish 
the truth, usefulness, optimality, or adoption of 
the surrounding theory. The corpus evidence 
documents a text-first source-of-truth architecture

Who signs, when the machine can write eve-
rything? 
Return to where the monograph began: a civiliza-

pause to judge. The preceding chapters of typed

the far end, like an elaborate machine for tidiness. 
They are not. They serve a declared normative 
governance commitment: consequential standing 
should remain attributable to an accountable hu-
man or institutionally constituted human authori-
ty, even when computation prepares the evidence 
and executes pre -authorized policy. That com-
mitment is not a theorem of computability; its le-
gitimacy must be defended in the affected 
institution and remains contestable. 
State the point at its highest level, one last time. 
Under the governance stance adopted here, the

architecture leaves the consequential act of war-
rant attributable to accountable human or institu-
tional authority. An automated system may 
execute a policy that was validly delegated, but ex-
ecution does not create the authority, legitimacy, 
or accountability of that delegation. The declared 
horizon, visible debt, and abstention machinery 
prepare a legible decision object; they do not 
manufacture the standing to bind people or insti-
tutions. 
The corpus gives this human -in-command pat-
tern a name — iKant — and the name is a disci-
pline against two opposite errors. It is not a moral 
subject: it holds no values of its own, only a nor-
mative kernel that some human wrote. It is not a 
metaphysical oracle: it does not know what is 
right; it detects where a case has turned hard, 
norm-laden, or self-contradictory, and escalates it. 
Mechanically it is a circuit -breaker over four 
things kept deliberately apart — a model of the 
world, a model of itself, a nor mative kernel, and 
an epistemic history — and its highest function is 
not to answer but to recognise the answers it must 
not give alone. A meta -controller that quietly de-

Recall the little word that has haunted the ar-

without ontological overreach — “must” — and

something is constructible, that it is stable for an

it exists necessarily in itself. Both an ambitious 
metaphysics and a confident machine can slide 
from the first of these to the last without ever

for forbidding the silent crossing and demanding, 
at the last and most tempting border, an explicit 
warrant or an honest abstention. Keeping the pen 
is what that grammar is for. It is the insistence that 
the signature under the final step — this claim 
may responsibly support this use — is a human 
signature, applied in daylight, answerable to those 
it binds.

that a person declares truth by signature; it is that 
the authorization of a claim for a named use must

CHAPTER 41  
Typed Domains, Epistem-
ic Horizons, and Reticula 
The formal core is intentionally local. It does not 
attempt a universal semantics of science or natural 
language. It fixes a finite or effectively presented 
operational domain and proves only what follows 
inside that domain. 
A level is a triple 
𝐿𝑖 = (𝑋𝑖, 𝛴𝑖, 𝑄𝑖), 
where 𝑋𝑖 is a state set, 𝛴𝑖 is a family of admitted 
partial effective operations or transition relations, 
and 𝑄𝑖 is a declared family of queries. A determin-
istic transmission is a typed map 𝜏: 𝑋 → 𝑌; a sto-
chastic transmission is a Markov kernel 𝐾: 𝑋 ⇝
𝑌. Side information, tolerances, and randomness 
policies are part of the transmission contract and 
may not be inferred silently. 
A horizon is the versioned tuple 
H = (S, Ω, Q, T, R, M, V, Π) 
where S is the admitted source manifest, Ω the 
scope, Q the query family, T the allowed trans-

## Page 294

The Accounting Laye r of Computationa l Semantics  
294 
formations, R the required receipts, M the sup-
port and contradiction rules, V the validation 
procedures, and Π the priority and conflict poli-
cy. Resource budgets and scheduling belong to 
the evaluator contract rather than to H. The tuple 
is a contract for a computation, not a claim about 
all reality. 
For a query family 𝑄 on 𝑋, define 
𝑥 ≡𝑄 𝑥′ ⇔ ∀𝑞 ∈ 𝑄, 𝑞(𝑥) = 𝑞(𝑥′). 
For approximate queries, equality is replaced by a 
declared metric and tolerance. A deterministic 
transmission 𝜏: 𝑋 → 𝑌 is 𝑄-faithful when 
𝜏(𝑥) = 𝜏(𝑥′) ⇒ 𝑥 ≡𝑄 𝑥′. 
This term replaces the historically useful but am-
biguous phrase quasi-injective. It states exactly 
which distinctions are preserved and does not 
suggest global recoverability.

and Recovery Conditions 
Credited standard result — Query Factoriza-
tion Theorem (F01) 
Let τ: X → Y and let Q be a family of queries q: X 
→ A_q. Define τ to be Q -faithful when τ(x) = 
τ(x′) implies q(x) = q(x′) for every q ∈ Q. The fol-
lowing are equivalent: (1) τ is Q -faithful; (2) for 
every q ∈ Q there exists a unique decoder q̄_q: 
im(τ) → A_q such that q = q̄_q ∘ τ. 
Proof. Assume Q -faithfulness. For y ∈ im(τ), 
choose x with τ(x)=y and set q̄_q(y)=q(x). If x′ is 
another preimage, Q -faithfulness gives q(x)=q(x′), 
so q̄_q is well defined; uniqueness follows because 
every y in im( τ) has a preimage. Conversely, if 
q=q̄_q∘τ and τ(x)=τ(x′), then 
q(x)=q̄_q(τ(x))=q̄_q(τ(x′))=q(x′). ∎ 
Boundary. The canonical decoder is defined on 
im(τ), not automatically on all of Y. A total exten-
sion Y → A_q requires an additional extension 
assumption, such as a chosen default when A_q is

CHAPTER 43  
Computability, Termina-
tion, and Formal Limits 
A compact reticulum  is a finite or effectively 
enumerable directed graph whose nodes are levels, 
whose edges are typed transmissions, and whose 
evaluation contract declares an effective scheduler, 
resource policy, terminal sum type, and horizon -
relative closure. “Closure” means that every in -
scope query is routed to an answer or a typed non-
answer; it does not mean that the reticulum con-
tains every truth about its domain. 
Local derived result — Bounded Reticular 
Evaluator (F05) 
Let C be an effectively encoded configuration 
space. Suppose the one -step transition dispatcher 
is partial recursive, the scheduler is computable, 
and every local operation or transmission is in-
voked through that dispatcher. Then the evalua-
tor obtained by iterating scheduled steps until a 
terminal is reached is a partial recursive function

## Page 300

The Accounting Laye r of Computationa l Semantics  
300 
from initial configurations to terminals and re-
ceipts. 
Proof. Encode configurations, scheduler state, 
and receipt prefixes as natural numbers. One 
scheduled step is partial recursive by hypothesis. 
Finite iteration is partial recursive by composition 
and primitive recursion; unbounded search for 
the first terminal is partial recursive by minimiza-
tion. If a local operation diverges, the evaluator is 
undefined, which is why F06 requires a stronger 
terminalized dispatcher. The result is a standard 
closure fact instantiated for CRC. ∎ 
Local derived result — Budgeted Totality in-
to Typed Terminal States (F06) 
Let Result(Y) = Answer(Y) + Unknown + Con-
tradiction + OutOfHorizon + Review + Timeout 
+ Failure. Assume a total computable dispatcher 
δ:C×{0,…,B}→Continue(C)+Result(Y) such that 
δ(c,0)=Timeout and every Continue(c′) returned 
at budget b>0 is followed only with budget b−1. 
Then the budgeted evaluator 
eval_B:C→Result(Y) is total computable. 
Proof. Induct on b. At b=0 the dispatcher re-
turns Timeout. At b>0, totality of δ yields either a

## Page 301

The Accounting Laye r of Computationa l Semantics

terminal or Continue(c′); in the second case the 
induction hypothesis applies at b−1. Computabil-
ity follows from bounded recursion. The premise 
is deliberately stronger than “local functions are 
computable”: every scheduled step must itself 
terminate or be wrapped by a terminating timeout 
or failure constructor. ∎ 
Credited standard reduction instantiated 
here — Propagation of Undecidability Under 
Query Factorization (F07) 
Let C be an effectively encoded promise domain 
and let P:C→{0,1} be undecidable as a promise 
problem. Let τ:C→Y be total computable. If 
there is a predicate P̄  on the promise set τ(C) such 
that P=P̄ ∘τ, then P̄  is undecidable on τ(C) relative 
to the induced representation. 
Proof. A decider for P̄  on the promised inputs 
τ(C) would decide P: on input x ∈C compute τ(x) 
and return P̄ (τ(x)). This contradicts undecidabil-

agates only when it factors through the 
transmission; it does not say that every property or 
every encoding preserves the difficulty. ∎

Let S=(X,→_S) and T=(Y,→_T) be source and 
target transition systems. A one -way simulation 
contract contains an encoding e:X→Y, a relation 
R⊆X×Y, paired observables (o_S,o_T) with a de-
clared metric d_o, a distortion bound ε_o for each 
observable, and a per -source-step overhead bound 
p:X→ℕ.

Credited standard simulation result instanti-

Assume (i) (x₀,e(x₀)) ∈R; (ii) whenever (x,y) ∈R 
and x→_S x′, there exists a target path 
y→_T^{≤p(x)}y′ with (x′,y′) ∈R; and (iii) for eve-
ry declared observable pair, 
d_o(o_S(x),o_T(y))≤ε_o whenever (x,y) ∈R. 
Then every finite source trace x₀→_S⋯→_S x_n 
has a related target trace with at most 
Σ_{i=0}^{n−1}p(x_i) target steps, and every 
paired state satisfies its declared pointwise distor-
tion bound. 
Proof. Induct on source -trace length. The base 
is the initialization relation. The step condition 
extends any related target prefix by a bounded tar-
get path and re -establishes R at the next source 
state. Summing the per-step bounds gives the total 
overhead; the observable condition holds at each 
paired state. No cumulative error claim follows 
unless a separate composition rule is supplied. ∎ 
Boundary. One-way simulation is not equiva-
lence. Bisimulation, robust decoding, perturba-
tion stability, and complexity preservation are 
separate obligations.

Non-entailment boundary proposition — Ex-

Let E(a) mean that a machine execution produced

Credited standard information result instan-
tiated here — Zero Conditional Query En-
tropy and Almost-Sure Recovery (F19) 
Let X be a finite -valued random variable, τ a de-
terministic transmission, and Q(X) the finite 
vector of answers to a declared query family. 
Then H(Q(X) | τ(X)) = 0 if and only if there ex-
ists a measurable decoder q̄ such that Q(X) = 
q̄(τ(X)) almost surely. 
Proof. For finite variables, zero conditional en-
tropy means that Q(X) is almost surely a func-
tion of τ(X); define q̄ on each positive -
probability fiber by that unique value. Converse-
ly, if such q̄ exists, Q(X) is determined by τ(X), 
so the conditional entropy is zero. Boundary. 
This is distribution -relative and almost -sure; it 
neither guarantees pointwise recovery outside 
the support nor converts Shannon information 
into warrant.

CHAPTER 47  
Reference Semantics for 
Epistemic Use Gates 
The gate is a deterministic policy interpreter over 
versioned inputs; it is not a learned confidence 
threshold. Its precedence is: 
1. verify horizon and policy versions; 
2. test horizon adequacy for the named use; 
3. reject out -of-scope, uncomputed, or un-
supported evidence states; 
4. route contradiction and unknown debt 
components to review; 
5. compare the debt vector componentwise 
with the use threshold vector; 
6. accept a typed discharge only for the com-
ponent, authority, scope, and version it 
names; 
7. evaluate waiver authority, scope, expiry, 
and residual risk; 
8. emit an integrity-protected receipt contain-
ing every input identifier and the complete 
blocking set.

## Page 325

The Accounting Laye r of Computationa l Semantics  
325 
The same precedence is the reference semantics: 
verify versions; test horizon adequacy; compute 
evidence status and debt; route unsupported, con-
tradictory, or unknown states; compare every debt 
component with the named -use threshold; then 
accept only a typed discharge or a valid bounded 
waiver. The emitted receipt records all input iden-
tifiers, the policy version, the complete blocking 
set, and the terminal outcome. 
The algorithm does not establish that the policy 
is legitimate or that the sources are true. It makes 
the policy application reconstructable and pre-
vents an evidence status from silently becoming a 
use authorization.

CHAPTER 48  
Threat Model and Trust-
ed Boundary 
The non -laundering guarantee depends on assets 
and attack surfaces that must be collected in one 
threat model. Assets are source identity, receipt 
integrity, dependency completeness, event order, 
policy and horizon identifiers, reviewer authority, 
waiver scope and expiry, monitor coverage, and 
user-visible status. Threats include forged or stale 
receipts, source-selection bias, omitted dependen-
cies, policy capture, privilege escalation, collusion 
between proposer and certifier, bypass of moni-
tored surfaces, optimistic defaults on unknown 
components, replay under superseded policy, se-
lective disclosure of blocking components, and 
interface relabelling of review as approval. 
Minimum controls are separation of roles, im-
mutable event identifiers, signed or integrity -
protected receipts, version pinning, revocation, 
complete blocking -set reporting, negative tests, 
fail-closed unknown semantics, contestation, and

## Page 328

The Accounting Laye r of Computationa l Semantics  
328 
an explicit bypass event. None of these controls 
proves source truth or institutional justice. They 
define the computational envelope within which 
the local safety theorem applies.

Appendix B — Epistemic 
Debt Vector Coding and 
Claim Falsification 
The nine debt components form a candidate cod-
ing instrument and are coded independently 
pending external reliability evidence. Severity is 
use-independent; use enters only through the gate 
threshold vector. The code set is 0 = obligation 
absent, 1 = documented and bounded caveat, 2 = 
material unresolved obligation, 3 = critical unre-
solved structural obligation, and U = unknown 
because the dependency record is insufficient. 
Under the strict conservative PropagationPolicy, 
U is absorbing on the declared relevance set; other 
profiles must be declared and receipted. At the 
gate, U is not compared numerically; it routes ac-
cording to the use contract, while Dependen-
cyCoverage remains a separate input. 
Source. Diagnostic question:  Can the origin 
be identified and admitted under the horizon? 
Typed repair:  Attach or exclude the source; 
recompute status.

Cross-Layer Necessity and Layer -
Removal Criterion 
The mandatory architecture is cumulative only if 
each interface exports something the next layer 
cannot safely reconstruct after the fact. RLA ex-
ports preserved and collapsed distinctions; CRC 
exports executable closure and terminal semantics; 
ECU/ECNN exports typed local epistemic ac-
tions and receipts; ROA exports observer and 
governance context; ED exports residual warrant 
and use standing. Bounded simulation is a side ob-
ligation, not a required export: it is introduced on-
ly when a cross -formalism claim needs an explicit 
simulation certificate. F23 converts the cumula-
tive intuition into a removal test: a layer may be 
replaced only when its complete interface export 
is effectively reconstructable from adjacent bun-
dles and every admitted query, terminal, receipt 
predicate, debt update, threat assumption, and 
resource bound remains unchanged. Failure of 
any condition is evidence that the layer is load -
bearing; success establishes only relative redun-
dancy under the frozen horizon, not unique min-
imality.

Methodological Note on 
Drafting Assisted by Artifi-
cial Intelligence 
Parts of drafting, restructuring, terminology har-
monization, bibliography expansion, figure proto-
typing, source-concept mining, finite-model stress 
testing, and local consistency checking were sup-
ported by AI -based assistants used as tools under 
human direction. The author remains responsible 
for every conceptual claim, theorem statement, 
formal choice, citation, interpretation, omission, 
and error. Generated material was treated as can-
didate artefact: it entered the manuscript only af-
ter source comparison, domain checks, hostile 
review, and human release approval. No AI sys-
tem is treated as an autonomous scientific author-
ity, certifier, or truth oracle.
